title: Space and Medical Physiology
blurb: An explorer of how the human body adapts to spaceflight, linking biomedical physiology, engineering, and mission operations.

person.name: Anand (Sunny) Narayanan
person.affiliation: Florida State University / FAMU-FSU College of Engineering
interests: research on the International Space Station

papers.title: Physiological Alterations in Relation to Space Flight: The Role of Nutrition

notes.takeaway: Spaceflight stressors alter physiology and nutrition can shape adaptation and recovery.
notes.why: It introduces the coupled biomedical systems problem.

papers.title: A systematic review and meta-analysis of bone loss in space travelers

notes.takeaway: Human space travelers show measurable microgravity-associated bone loss across missions.
notes.why: It grounds skeletal risk in an evidence synthesis rather than a guessed DOI.

papers.title: How does spaceflight affect the acquired immune system?

notes.takeaway: Spaceflight changes immune regulation through interacting environmental and physiological stressors.
notes.why: It broadens the foundations beyond a single organ system.

papers.title: Radiation-associated cardiovascular risks for future deep-space missions

notes.takeaway: Deep-space radiation creates cardiovascular concerns that differ from ordinary orbital exposure.
notes.why: It connects mission environment to specific human-health risk.

papers.title: Validation of a New Rodent Experimental System to Investigate Consequences of Long Duration Space Habitation

notes.takeaway: Validated animal systems allow long-duration habitation risks to be studied under controlled conditions.
notes.why: Models are necessary when astronaut cohorts remain small.

papers.title: A spacecraft-compatible combined artificial gravity and exercise (CAGE) system to sustain astronaut health in the next generation of long-term spaceflight

notes.takeaway: Artificial gravity and exercise can be designed as an integrated countermeasure system.
notes.why: It links physiology to engineering and mission operations.

papers.title: Integrated RNA-seq Analysis Indicates Asynchrony in Clock Genes between Tissues under Spaceflight

notes.takeaway: Spaceflight can desynchronize molecular timing across tissues in model organisms.
notes.why: It illustrates why multi-tissue, longitudinal data matter.

papers.title: Effect of simulated microgravity and ionizing radiation on expression profiles of miRNA, lncRNA, and mRNA in human lymphoblastoid cells

notes.takeaway: Microgravity and radiation together alter regulatory RNA expression profiles.
notes.why: Combined stressors are central to deep-space physiology.

papers.title: Why Personalized Medicine Is the Frontier of Medicine and Performance for Humans in Space

notes.takeaway: Individual baselines and responses matter when crews face long missions.

papers.title: Basic principles and concept design of a real-time clinical decision support system for managing medical emergencies on missions to Mars

notes.takeaway: Decision support can help crews manage medical emergencies when Earth-based care is delayed.
notes.why: It gives the predictive frontier an operational setting.

papers.title: The final frontier: health in space

notes.takeaway: Space medicine combines environmental, physiological, psychological, and operational hazards.
notes.why: It provides a systems-level risk map.

papers.title: Progress in Space Medicine Research on China Space Station

notes.takeaway: Long-duration station research provides a continuing platform for human-spaceflight medicine.
notes.why: It connects orbital experiments to future exploration health systems.

sections.label: Foundations: altered gravity and the body
sections.summary: Fluid shifts, skeletal unloading, and cardiovascular control establish the physiological baseline. Ground experiments and flight observations help distinguish responses to unloading from changes associated with confinement, diet, and mission duration.
questions: Which countermeasure combinations work across systems?

sections.label: From mechanism to mission risk
sections.summary: Radiation, immune change, neuro-ocular effects, and bone loss become operational constraints. The field moves from describing individual responses to deciding which changes require monitoring, countermeasures, or limits on exposure.
questions: How should risks be modeled when missions last years?

sections.label: Integrated human data
sections.summary: Longitudinal omics and shared repositories connect organ systems and missions. Comparisons across tissues and time points can reveal shared responses, while small cohorts and differences between missions constrain causal interpretation.
questions: What data standards preserve useful individual differences?

sections.label: Frontier: prediction with context
sections.summary: Machine learning and mission platforms promise earlier detection while raising questions about causation and transfer.
questions: Can models generalize from ISS crews to lunar and Mars missions?

opportunities: Causal models of combined spaceflight stressors
Build longitudinal designs that separate gravity, radiation, confinement, exercise, and diet effects.
Test whether multi-organ biomarkers can guide crew-specific interventions.
Pair standardized space-biology metadata with transparent model validation.

podcast.title: The Body in Orbit: Anand (Sunny) Narayanan's Space Physiology
podcast.description: A guided path from altered gravity and bone loss to integrated astronaut data and predictive health models.
